blocks.text: Final Exam - 10 critical questions covering Lesson 1-10
These 10 questions cover every lesson. Options are very close - think like production developer. You need 80% to earn HTML certificate and prove you can build complete websites and apps.

blocks.question:
Lesson 1+7: You have

My Portfolio

Content. Page shows Content but h1 style broken in some browsers and SEO suffers. What are two critical errors covering structure and semantics?
options: h1 inside head is invalid - visible content must be in body, head only for metadata; and missing semantic header/main - h1 should be inside header inside body, not head, for correct document outline and SEO
h1 should be inside title tag, so <h1>My Portfolio</h1> is correct fix for SEO
Error is missing lang attribute and missing <!DOCTYPE html>, h1 in head is allowed in HTML5
No error, h1 in head is modern pattern for SEO, Google prefers h1 in head for faster indexing
blocks.correctFeedback: Lesson 1 foundation! Head = invisible metadata, body = visible. Semantic header contains h1.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Where should visible h1 live? Head or body? What does head contain?
blocks.reasoning: Head contains metadata only (title, meta). Visible content like h1 must be in body, ideally in header element. Placing in head breaks rendering and SEO.

blocks.question: Lesson 2: You need to show warning 'Do not share password!' with strong importance, and technical term HTML in italic without importance. Which is semantically correct and why b vs strong matters?
options: Do not share password! and HTML because b and i are newer and strong/em are deprecated in HTML5

Do not share password! because strong conveys semantic importance that screen readers announce with emphasis, and HTML for technical term with no extra importance - b is purely visual bold with no semantic importance while strong is importance
Do not share password! for warning and HTML for technical term because mark is for warnings

Do not share password!

and

HTML

separate paragraphs because warnings and terms must be in separate p tags
blocks.correctFeedback: Lesson 2 mastery! Strong = importance, b = visual only. Em = stress emphasis, i = technical term/style.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Which conveys importance to assistive tech - b or strong? Which is purely presentational?
blocks.reasoning: Strong has semantic importance, announced by screen readers. B is presentational bold only. I is stylistic italic for technical terms, em is stress emphasis.

blocks.question: Lesson 3: File structure: index.html at root, projects/app.html inside folder. From app.html you link to root index.html with <a href="index.html"> and to external site with <a href="https://github.com" target="_blank"> without rel. What are two bugs?
options: First link should be /index.html not index.html because index.html only works from root, and target _blank without rel is safe so no bug second

Bug 1: Relative path index.html from projects/app.html points to projects/index.html not root, correct is ../index.html to go up one level. Bug 2: target=_blank without rel=noopener noreferrer allows tabnabbing attack where new page can access window.opener and redirect original page - security vulnerability
Bug 1: Should use absolute path C:\index.html for root, Bug 2: target _blank is deprecated should use target _new
No bugs, both links are correct and secure for production complete websites
blocks.correctFeedback: Lesson 3 path and security! ../ and rel are mandatory for production navigation.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Visualize folders: app.html inside projects/. Where does index.html search? What does window.opener allow?
blocks.reasoning: From projects/app.html, index.html resolves to projects/index.html. Need ../ to go up. target=_blank gives window.opener access, need noopener noreferrer for security.

blocks.question: Lesson 4+9: You add without alt, width, height, loading. It looks fine. Why will Lighthouse performance and accessibility scores fail and what is production fix?
options: Will pass because src is enough, alt width height loading are optional for jpg images and only required for png

Fails accessibility because alt missing - screen readers need description; fails performance because no width/height causes CLS layout shift hurting SEO, and no loading=lazy loads image immediately even offscreen wasting data on mobile. Fix: alt meaningful description or empty for decorative, width height to prevent CLS, loading=lazy for offscreen images
Fails because hero.jpg must be absolute URL not relative, and must have title attribute not alt, fix with title and absolute URL
Fails because img must be inside figure always, without figure img is invalid, fix by wrapping in figure
blocks.correctFeedback: Lesson 4+9 combined! Alt, width/height CLS, loading lazy are production must-haves.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: What does missing alt cause for blind users? What does missing width/height cause for layout? What does no lazy cause for data?
blocks.reasoning: Alt mandatory for accessibility, width/height prevent CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift) ranking factor, loading=lazy defers offscreen images saving data.

blocks.question: Lesson 6: You build contact form with <input type="text" placeholder="Email"> no label, radio buttons with different name attributes so user can select all, and form method GET for sending message. What are three critical bugs?
options: No bugs, placeholder replaces label, different names for radios is correct for multiple selection, GET is correct for contact messages

Bug1: Placeholder not label - disappears on type, not reliably announced, fails WCAG - need label with for/id. Bug2: Radios with different names are separate groups allowing multiple selection, same name groups them for single choice. Bug3: GET puts data in URL visible and limited length, should be POST for creating/sending messages with data in body not URL
Bug1: Should use type email not text, Bug2: Should use checkbox not radio, Bug3: Should use action POST not method POST
Bug1: Placeholder should be title not placeholder, Bug2: Radios need checked attribute, Bug3: GET and POST are same no difference
blocks.correctFeedback: Lesson 6 form mastery! Label, radio grouping, GET vs POST are core for interactive websites and apps.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Does placeholder persist after typing? How does browser group radios? Where does GET put data?
blocks.reasoning: Label required not placeholder, radio grouping by name attribute same name = one group, GET for retrieval URL visible, POST for submission body not visible.

blocks.question: Lesson 7: You build complete website with <div id="header">, <div id="nav">, <div id="main"> with two <main> tags, <div class="section"> without heading, and <div id="footer">. Why is this non-semantic and invalid?
options: It's semantic and valid, div with id is same as header/nav/main/section/footer and multiple mains are allowed for different sections

Div is non-semantic generic container with no meaning for SEO/screen readers, should use header/nav/main/section/footer landmarks; only one main per page allowed containing main content not header/footer; section should have heading h2-h6 to define theme, otherwise use div for styling wrapper only
Div is semantic and header/nav are non-semantic, so div version is actually better for SEO, and multiple mains improve SEO
Only error is missing lang attribute, div structure is correct and professional for complete websites
blocks.correctFeedback: Lesson 7 semantic mastery! Div soup vs landmarks is difference between junior and professional websites.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: What does header/nav/main provide that div doesn't? How many main contents can page have? Does section need heading?
blocks.reasoning: Semantic elements provide landmarks for SEO and accessibility. Only one main per page, not inside header/footer. Section is thematic grouping needs heading, else div.

blocks.question: Lesson 8: You share complete website link on WhatsApp - shows plain URL no image. FAQ uses div+JS click to expand. Video iframe <iframe src="youtube.com/embed/..."></iframe> no title and loads immediately slowing page. What are three modern fixes?
options: Add for WhatsApp preview, use <p> for FAQ, add alt to iframe for accessibility

Fix1: Add OG meta og:title og:description og:image and twitter card for rich preview when shared - controls WhatsApp/Facebook preview. Fix2: Use native details/summary for FAQ - accessible, no JS, keyboard and screen reader announce expanded state. Fix3: Iframe needs title for accessibility mandatory and loading=lazy to defer offscreen loading improving performance
Fix1: Add img tag at top for WhatsApp, Fix2: FAQ div is correct no need details, Fix3: Iframe should have preload none not loading lazy
No fixes needed, WhatsApp preview is automatic, div FAQ is modern pattern, iframe without title is valid for performance
blocks.correctFeedback: Lesson 8 modern! OG tags, details/summary, iframe title+lazy are production modern website must-haves.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: What controls social sharing preview? What native element provides FAQ accordion? What does iframe need for screen readers and performance?
blocks.reasoning: OG tags control social previews, details/summary is native accessible disclosure widget, iframe requires title for a11y and loading=lazy for performance.

blocks.question:
Lesson 9: You build complete website with
Send
as button, no skip link, 15 nav links, images with important text inside image like where image says Welcome. What are three accessibility failures?
options: No failures, div onclick is accessible button pattern, no need skip link if nav is short, text inside images is good for design

Fail1: Div not focusable nor announced as button - need semantic button or tabindex 0 + role button + Enter/Space handlers, but button element is best. Fail2: No skip link forces keyboard users Tab 15 times every page to reach main - need skip link first element linking to main. Fail3: Text inside image with empty alt hides text from screen readers - important text must be real HTML not image pixels, alt empty only for decorative
Fail1: Should use span not div for button, Fail2: Skip link should be at bottom, Fail3: Alt should be file name welcome.png for text images
Fail1: Div needs alt like img, Fail2: Skip link needs JavaScript, Fail3: Text inside images needs title attribute
blocks.correctFeedback: Lesson 9 a11y mastery! Button semantics, skip link, text in images are critical for inclusive complete websites and apps.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Can keyboard Tab to div? What does skip link do? Can screen reader read text inside jpg?
blocks.reasoning: Div not natively focusable/button, skip link bypasses repeated nav for keyboard users WCAG requirement, text inside images fails because screen readers can't read pixels and needs real HTML text.

blocks.question: Lesson 10 Final: You deploy complete website but W3C validator shows errors, Lighthouse accessibility 60, performance 50, SEO 70, and keyboard Tab can't reach contact form. What is final production checklist to reach 90+ scores before sharing with clients?
options: Ignore validator and Lighthouse, scores don't matter for clients, keyboard not important if mouse works, just share link

Checklist: 1) Fix W3C errors - valid HTML mandatory 2) All images alt + width/height + loading lazy 3) All inputs labels with for/id 4) One h1, hierarchy h1->h2->h3 5) Semantic header/nav/main/section/article/footer 6) Skip link first element 7) Lang and viewport meta 8) OG meta for sharing 9) Iframes title + lazy 10) Keyboard test Tab through all interactive elements must be focusable and operable with Enter/Space - this makes complete website production ready for real clients and employers
Only need to add CSS to improve Lighthouse scores, HTML doesn't affect scores, so add more colors
Need to add more divs to improve structure, divs improve Lighthouse accessibility and SEO scores
blocks.correctFeedback: Perfect final exam! You now know complete production checklist for complete websites and apps that serve real users. You are ready to build and deploy!
blocks.incorrectFeedback: What makes website valid, accessible, performant, SEO ready, keyboard operable?
blocks.reasoning: Production checklist covers validation, accessibility alt/labels/semantics/skip link/keyboard, performance width/height/lazy, SEO meta OG hierarchy, all required for professional complete websites and apps.
